claim: Self-guided castle tours last about an hour, 1.5 hours with audioguide; the esplanade has a free parking lot with around fifty spaces and additional free parking is available in town if needed.
quote: Self-guided tours last around an hour... The esplanade of Bouillon Castle has a free parking lot with around fifty spaces

claim: Falconry shows run Feb 22-Nov 11 at 11:30, 14:00 and 15:30 with an extra 17:00 show on weekends in April/May/June/September and daily in July/August; each show lasts about 30 minutes and is included in castle admission.
quote: Falconry shows... take place at 11:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m., and 3:30 p.m., with an additional 5:00 p.m. show on weekends in April, May, June, and September

claim: The Bouillon City Pass is a single combo ticket covering the Château fort, Archéoscope (Bouillon Medieval Experience) and Musée Ducal; in high season (Apr 1-Nov 11 2026) the City Pass+ adds the L'Odyssée de Lumière night show and costs €16 adult / €12 child/student.
quote: Bouillon City Pass+ (which includes the pass plus the 'L'Odyssée de Lumière' night show at the castle) costs Adults and 65+: €16 - Students and children: €12

claim: Bouillon Castle holds 4.4/5 across 1,565 TripAdvisor reviews; visitors praise the medieval atmosphere, secret passages, panoramic Semois views and falconry shows, while common complaints are the steep uphill walk and numerous stairs, occasional weather-cancelled falconry shows, and that the City Pass bundles attractions automatically.
quote: Overall Rating: 4.4 of 5 bubbles (1,565 reviews)... Steep uphill walk and numerous stairs to reach the castle... Automatic 'pass' bundling discourages single-attraction visits

claim: The Musée Ducal rates only 3.7/5 across 68 TripAdvisor reviews; visitors estimate 30-60 minutes for the visit, praise the crusades artifacts and local ironwork displays but complain about limited English signage and inflexible ticket-desk staff.
quote: Overall Rating: 3.7 out of 5 bubbles (68 reviews)... Limited English materials... Reviewers estimate 30-60 minutes for a complete visit

claim: The renovated Bouillon Medieval Experience (Archéoscope) scores 4.3/5 on TripAdvisor with praise for immersive audiovisual scenography, multilingual personal-headphone audio guides and friendly staff, but reviewers note the content is heavily about the First Crusade rather than Godefroid himself and recommend it for ages 9+.
quote: Overall Rating: 4.3 out of 5 stars (19 reviews)... Audio guide system allowing multilingual access simultaneously via personal headphones... it's better for ages 9+

claim: The Tombeau du Géant at Botassart is classified as 'exceptional heritage of Wallonia' — a wooded hill in a meander of the Semois forming a monumental sarcophagus shape, and is one of Belgium's most photographed landscapes.
quote: The Giant's Tomb is an exceptional geomorphosite classified as 'exceptional heritage of Wallonia' located in Botassart, municipality of Bouillon

claim: Free parking is available at the Botassart belvedere with the viewpoint reachable in a few minutes' walk without difficulty; refreshment bar and restrooms only open in July-August, and access is free 24/7 year-round.
quote: Free parking is available on-site in Botassart... accessible from the parking lot 'in a few minutes' walk, without difficulty'... Refreshment bar and restrooms available in high season (July-August)

claim: The Pont de Liège in Bouillon was first mentioned in 1069 as a wooden bridge linking Germany to France, rebuilt in stone in 1598 and reinforced by Vauban in 1680; the current bridge dates from 1951 and sits opposite the Hôtel de la Poste.
quote: Le Pont de Liège... face à l'Hôtel de la Poste... première mention en 1069... reconstruit en pierre en 1598... renforcé par Vauban en 1680... pont actuel date de 1951

claim: Bouillon's architectural promenade starts from the tourist office in the former Sépulcrines convent (1626) on the Quai des Saulx, follows Boulevard Heynen along the Semois, crosses the Pont de Liège and loops back below the castle ramparts.
quote: promenade architecturale... Quai des Saulx... ancien couvent des Sépulcrines (1626)... boulevard Heynen le long de la Semois... Pont de Liège
